newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat ends lower on rain forecasts.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat ends lower on rain forecasts.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures settled lower amid increasing chances for moisture early next week in dry areas of the northern U.S. Plains, traders said.

Spring wheat had been supported at the midsession on concern over dryness in the northern U.S. Plains and on spillover strength from CBOT soybeans, traders said. But updated weather forecasts were revised to include more rain in spring wheat areas and soybeans fell back from their intraday highs.
"It looks now like there's a 50 to 60 percent chance for maybe 1/4 to 1/2 inch of rain Sunday into Monday," a trader said after the close.
MGE spring wheat settled 3-1/4 to 6-1/2 cents per bushel lower, with July down 3-1/4 cents at $3.98-1/4. New crop September lost 3-1/2 cents to close at $3.89-3/4.
Featured players included Benson-Quinn, which bought 1.6 million Sept bushels and sold 500,000 July. Atwood-Peavey sold 1.5 million July.
